From eb101d2abdcccb514ca4fccd3b278dd8267374f6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Fedor Pchelkin <pchelkin@ispras.ru>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 12:47:30 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] wifi: rtw88: check for PCI upstream bridge existence

pci_upstream_bridge() returns NULL if the device is on a root bus.  If
8821CE is installed in the system with such a PCI topology, the probing
routine will crash.  This has probably been unnoticed as 8821CE is mostly
supplied in laptops where there is a PCI-to-PCI bridge located upstream
from the device.  However the card might be installed on a system with
different configuration.

Check if the bridge does exist for the specific workaround to be applied.

Found by Linux Verification Center (linuxtesting.org) with Svace static
analysis tool.

Fixes: 24f5e38a13b5 ("rtw88: Disable PCIe ASPM while doing NAPI poll on 8821CE")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Fedor Pchelkin <pchelkin@ispras.ru>
Acked-by: Ping-Ke Shih <pkshih@realtek.com>
Signed-off-by: Ping-Ke Shih <pkshih@realtek.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260220094730.49791-1-pchelkin@ispras.ru

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtw88/pci.c b/drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtw88/pci.c
index 56b16186d3aa..ec0a45bfb670 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtw88/pci.c
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtw88/pci.c
@@ -1804,7 +1804,8 @@ int rtw_pci_probe(struct pci_dev *pdev,
 	}
 
 	/* Disable PCIe ASPM L1 while doing NAPI poll for 8821CE */
-	if (rtwdev->chip->id == RTW_CHIP_TYPE_8821C && bridge->vendor == PCI_VENDOR_ID_INTEL)
+	if (rtwdev->chip->id == RTW_CHIP_TYPE_8821C &&
+	    bridge && bridge->vendor == PCI_VENDOR_ID_INTEL)
 		rtwpci->rx_no_aspm = true;
 
 	rtw_pci_phy_cfg(rtwdev);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch addresses a potential NULL pointer dereference in `rtw88/pci.c`. The modification adds a check for the existence of the PCI upstream bridge before accessing its vendor ID, ensuring that the workaround for 8821CE is only applied when a bridge actually exists.

## Modifications per file

- **drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtw88/pci.c**  
  Changed line 1807: the condition `bridge->vendor == PCI_VENDOR_ID_INTEL` is now guarded by a NULL check for `bridge`. The updated condition reads:  
  `if (rtwdev->chip->id == RTW_CHIP_TYPE_8821C && bridge && bridge->vendor == PCI_VENDOR_ID_INTEL)`

## Relationships between modifications

Only one file is changed, and the modification is isolated to a single conditional expression. No cross-file dependencies exist. The fix ensures safe access to `bridge->vendor` when `pci_upstream_bridge()` might return `NULL` (e.g., if the device is on a root bus).

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
struct pci_dev *bridge = pci_upstream_bridge(pdev);
if (rtwdev->chip->id == RTW_CHIP_TYPE_8821C && bridge->vendor == PCI_VENDOR_ID_INTEL)
Reason:
`pci_upstream_bridge()` returns NULL when the PCI device is on a root bus. The subsequent dereference of `bridge->vendor` without a NULL check causes a NULL pointer dereference and a crash during probing.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (rtwdev->chip->id == RTW_CHIP_TYPE_8821C &&
    bridge && bridge->vendor == PCI_VENDOR_ID_INTEL)
Reason:
Adding the `bridge &&` condition ensures the vendor check is only performed when `bridge` is not NULL, preventing the NULL pointer dereference.
